raw.translational: Understanding the shared role of glucose metabolism and PPARgamma signaling in both monogenic MODY2 and polygenic Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus can inform therapeutic strategies. While MODY2 is typically managed with diet and exercise due to impaired glucose sensing, insights into PPARgamma activation could offer avenues for managing insulin resistance in Type 2 Diabetes, potentially leading to synergistic or complementary treatments. However, the differing primary genetic etiologies suggest that therapies targeting downstream pathways may be more fruitful for shared benefit than targeting the primary causal genes directly.

partners.mechanism_chain: GCK (HGNC:4195) —PRODUCES→ Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17177); Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17177) —LEADS_TO→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337) —DECREASES→ Insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-150217); Insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-150217) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperglycemia (HP:0003124); Insulin secretion (REACT:R-HSA-150217) —LEADS_TO→ Neonatal diabetes mellitus (HP:0011330). Mutations in GCK impair its ability to phosphorylate glucose, leading to reduced glucose-6-phosphate production. This deficiency impacts glycolysis and subsequently impairs insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells. In MODY2, haploinsufficiency leads to a milder, later-onset hyperglycemia. In PNDM1, complete loss-of-function mutations result in a severe reduction in insulin secretion, manifesting as neonatal diabetes.

partners.mechanism_chain: GCK (HGNC:4209) —DECREASES→ Glucose (CHEBI:17234); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —DISRUPTS→ Insulin Secretion Regulation (GO:0043619); Insulin Secretion Regulation (GO:0043619) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperglycemia (HP:0003071); NDC1 (HGNC:29656) —DISRUPTS→ Nuclear Pore Complex Function (GO:0005643); Nuclear Pore Complex Function (GO:0005643) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665); Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental delay (HP:0001263); Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665) —LEADS_TO→ Achalasia (HP:0002072); Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665) —LEADS_TO→ Polyneuropathy (HP:0000750); Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665) —LEADS_TO→ Alacrima (HP:0000610); Glucose (CHEBI:17234) —INCREASES→ Neuronal Development and Function (GO:0048665). Loss of function in GCK impairs glucose phosphorylation, leading to reduced insulin secretion and hyperglycemia (MODY2). Separately, loss of function in NDC1 disrupts nuclear pore complex function, impacting neuronal development and function, which manifests as neurodevelopmental delay, achalasia, polyneuropathy, and alacrima.
